similar_scenes.name: Rick James
similar_scenes.book: Funk: The Music, the People, and the Rhythm of the One
similar_scenes.author: Rickey Vincent
similar_scenes.desc: James Ambrose Johnson Jr., criado por su madre en Búfalo, recadero de apuestas a los quince, desertor de la marina, huido a Canadá y Londres, llevó a Motown un funk sucio, intenso y peligroso. El primero en quitarle la corona a P-Funk, con sexo, drogas e irresponsabilidad: «You and I», «Mary Jane», «Bustin’ Out», «Love Gun». Street Songs (1981), su cima: «Give It to Me Baby» definió la nueva guarrería del R&B y fue el principio del fin; «Super Freak», de ritmo new wave (base de «U Can’t Touch This» de MC Hammer), el dúo «Fire and Desire» con Teena Marie y crónica callejera como «Ghetto Life» o «Mr. Policeman», que anticipaba el gangsta rap. Su Stone City Band mantuvo los solos de viento. Luego «Standing on the Top», «Cold Blooded», las Mary Jane Girls («All Night Long») y la caída, hasta la cárcel de Folsom.

similar_scenes.name: Punk funk neoyorquino: 99 Records, ESG y Liquid Liquid
similar_scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
similar_scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
similar_scenes.desc: El sello de la tienda anglófila de Ed Bahlman, con producción más cruda que ZE: ESG, las hermanas Scroggins del Bronx, funk ultraminimalista («apenas algunos golpes con un par de palillos y una simple melodía de bajo»), que Tony Wilson graba con Martin Hannett («Moody», «UFO»), luego adoptado por el house y sampleado por el rap. Liquid Liquid, percusión latina del Lower East Side y Fela Kuti («Cavern», plagiada en «White Lines» de Grandmaster Flash). Bush Tetras de Pat Place («Too Many Creeps»: «ritmo y paranoia»), Y Pants y el single de Vivien Goldman con Keith Levene.

podcast.title: Genre of Fishbone
podcast.body: Fishbone is identified as a band known for its punk funk style. "There was the punk funk of fishbone."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Hybrid Genre of the 1990s
podcast.body: Punk funk was identified as one of the hybrid genres evolving in the first half of the 1990s. "While all this stuff was going on with punk funk and funk metal and hybrids of punk grunge, metal and hip-hop in the first half of the 1990s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Hybrid Post-Punk Genre
podcast.body: Punk funk was a popular name for a danceable post-punk sound at the dawn of the 1980s, incorporating a funky rhythm section and other elements from new wave, Kraut Rock, funk, rap, and Jamaican dub, sometimes co-opting the "four on the floor" disco beat. "This post-punk genre was known by a number of names. Disco punk, techno punk, dance punk, and punk punk."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Post-Punk Explosion Part 7: All the rest

podcast.title: Influence of Public Image Limited
podcast.body: Public Image Limited significantly influenced the punk funk genre, and many bands recognized their pioneering role. "He hung out with some funk musicians, and eventually pulled together a band that ended up having a profound effect on several genres of music, including industrial and punk funk."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Reunions: Some Lasted....and Sadly, Some Didn't ｜ Part 2

podcast.title: Red Hot Chili Peppers' Success Formula
podcast.body: The Red Hot Chili Peppers decided to return to their "punk funk" approach, which had made their "Blood Sugar Sex Magik" album successful, for the recording of "Californication." "So it was decided that the peppers would go back to the approach of blood sugar sex magic. In other words, the punk funk that made them successful in the first place."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Long Strange Trip of John Frusciante Part 2

podcast.title: Rejected Band Idea
podcast.body: Rivers Cuomo was "talked out of forming" a punk funk band in the early 1990s. He was concerned that this genre choice might hinder the band's chances, especially at a time when the alternative music scene prioritized authenticity. "Rivers had been talked out of forming a punk funk band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 1
